topic: Female Reproductive System and Menstrual Cycle
key_concepts: Menstruation is the periodic shedding of blood and tissue from the uterine lining
A regular menstrual cycle lasts about 28 days
Ovulation occurs around day 14 and releases a mature egg from an ovary
Fertilization normally occurs in the fallopian tube
Ovaries produce ova and secrete estrogen and progesterone
Estrogen is responsible for typical female sexual characteristics
Progesterone prepares and maintains the uterus for pregnancy
FSH helps control the menstrual cycle and stimulates egg growth in the ovaries
Negative feedback keeps FSH, LH, estrogen, and progesterone levels relatively stable
The follicular phase thickens the uterine lining and develops an egg in the ovary
The luteal phase follows ovulation and lasts until the next period
Sperm can survive up to five days while an ovum survives 12 to 24 hours after ovulation
